label: Add or replace
gloss: write the row, or replace it if it is already there - so running twice makes one
why: Things arrive twice: an email is re-sent, a run is retried after a timeout, someone clicks Submit again. A flow that always adds a row turns every repeat into a duplicate - two records for one hire, two laptops ordered. Add or replace checks the key first: new key, new row; known key, same row. That property has a name, idempotent: running it twice leaves the same result as running it once.
cue: ask 'what happens if this runs twice?' - if the answer is 'two of everything', make the write add-or-replace
task: The same offer arrived twice. Keep one onboarding record for H-1, however many times it arrives.
notes: Try 'add a new row' first: two records for one person.
The key is the field that says two rows are the same thing.

checks.label: One record for H-1, not two
